title: Localization of Hom for completed lisse lattices
statement: For a base P and an IntegralComparison I as in [def-per-lisse-completed-system-data], for two reconstructed lattices there is a unique additive map from E tensor_A Hom of their normalized etale systems to rational sheaf Hom, sending a pure tensor a tensor f to scalar extension of I.inverse(f) followed by multiplication by a. This additive map is bijective. It asserts no site descent or existence of an integral comparison.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) and (4), with Corollary 5.1.5 for classical finite local systems; the comparison maps are reduction, inverse limit and localization. Their pullback and coefficient-extension compatibilities use these same maps. Etale-local existence of lattices is cited separately as an existing DAG node.

proof.text: Ordinary scalar extension carries each finite local basis to the same basis over the rational coefficient sheaf. For integral lisse modules $M,N$, form $H=\mathcal Hom_{B_X}(M,N)$ using [def-pur-sheaf-hom], so $H(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{B_X}(M,N)$. Let $H[1/\varpi]$ denote the sheaf colimit of $H\xrightarrow{\varpi}H\xrightarrow{\varpi}\cdots$, whose existence and sheafified sectionwise description are [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2). There is a canonical map to $\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(M[1/\varpi],N[1/\varpi])$, sending a map in stage $k$ to $\varpi^{-k}$ times its scalar extension. It is an isomorphism: on a common trivializing covering for $M=B_X^r$ and $N=B_X^s$, it is the coordinate map from the localization of the finite matrix module $B_X^{sr}$ to $E_X^{sr}$, with inverse obtained by writing its finitely many entries as local fractions and taking a common exponent. The maps agree on overlaps because they are the specified scalar-extension map. This also treats $r=0$ or $s=0$.

A Noetherian underlying space is quasi-compact, and every open subspace is quasi-compact; in particular intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact. Thus $X$ satisfies the qcqs hypothesis of [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections]. Apply it with $\mathcal R=B_X$, $U=X$, $I=\mathbf N$, and the diagram of degree-zero complexes $H\xrightarrow{\varpi}H\to\cdots$; the uniform lower bound is $a=0$ and take $q=0$. Together with step 5 it gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{B_X}(M,N)[1/\varpi]\cong H[1/\varpi](X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{E_X}(M[1/\varpi],N[1/\varpi]).$$
Here the first term is the module localization, equivalently $E\otimes_A\operatorname{Hom}_{B_X}(M,N)$. The map sends $\varpi^{-k}f$ to $\varpi^{-k}(1\otimes f)$, so it is precisely the Hom map from the raw rational category of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](2), restricted to the finite-free towers in step 4. It respects identity and composition because scalar multiplication does. This proves full faithfulness; it requires no assertion that every rational lisse sheaf has a global integral lattice. The supplied integral equivalence identifies integral Hom groups, and its scalar projection equations make this identification A-linear. Extend the resulting balanced map to E tensor_A Hom. Generation by pure tensors proves uniqueness of the additive map, including zero rank.

from.place: Localization of Hom for completed lisse lattices in the completed lisse comparison used to construct adic geometric fibres.

lean.statement:
theorem completed_lisse_rational_hom (P : Base.{u} l) (I : IntegralComparison l P) :
    ∀ F G : RawRational l P,
        ∃! h : (F.obj ⟶ G.obj) →+
            (rationalizedLattice l P I F ⟶ rationalizedLattice l P I G),
          Function.Bijective h ∧
          ∀ (a : P.E) (f : F.obj.integral ⟶ G.obj.integral),
            h (TensorProduct.tmul (Integers l P) a f) =
              (completedAdicChange P.X
                (I.coefficientIso.inv ≫ lisseIntegerToFieldSized l P.E P.X)).map
                  (I.equivalence.inverse.map ⟨f⟩).hom ≫
                    rationalScalar l P _ a
